cohort: Nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies at ≥36 weeks' gestation who received oxytocin and reached the second stage of labor
finding: While both increasing BMI and oxytocin dosage are associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, puerperal infection, and a composite of neonatal morbidities, there was no significant interaction between BMI and oxytocin dosage for any outcome.
